sources.title: Exact rational coordinates and degree example
sources.details: For L=8 and N=L_prime, x_m=8m/N for integer 0<=m<N; x_(N-1)=8-8/N<8 and spacing=8/N. N=16 gives 1/2 steps and endpoint15/2; N=24 gives1/3 steps and endpoint23/3. For a toy60°/unit rotation, position2 gives120° before and60° after; gap15 becomes15/2. Degrees were explicitly converted to radians for cos/sin; see verification_code and measurements.

claims.statement: Position Interpolation rescales each index m by L/L_prime before RoPE; the original function is evaluated at fractional coordinates and token content is retained.
claims.scope: RoPE coordinate transformation illustrated with L=8 and L_prime=16. Does not assert prior training at every fractional point or preservation of model task quality.

evidence.locator: §2.1 Eq1–2 (PDF p.3), §2.3 Eq4 and following paragraph (p.4); extracted lines134–158,236–252
evidence.supports: Eq4 is f_prime(x,m)=f(x,mL/L_prime), with positions mapped from [0,L_prime) to [0,L); Eq1 uses m times frequency. There is no token removal operation, and §3.1 retains the model architecture apart from rescaling.

claims.statement: The 16-card example maps 0,1,2,14,15 to0,0.5,1,7,7.5; all16 distinct coordinates remain below8. The24-card exercise gives5/3 and23/3, approximately1.6667 and7.6667. The60-degree toy gives120→60 degrees at position2 and gap15→7.5.

claims.scope: Exact hand-sized coordinate and rotation arithmetic, and the rendered diagram. Cardinality is coordinate/card count, not a model task-score denominator; no training or model evaluation.
